A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Beyond Blur: A Fluid Perspective on Generative Diffusion Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and reformatted content.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original FFHQ and MNIST generation and interpolation experiments, including FID and LPIPS measurements across Peclet numbers.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds FFHQ precision, recall, density, and coverage measurements, plus LSUN Church generation and interpolation results.

M1.justification: The advection-diffusion corruption, spectral turbulence generator, Lattice Boltzmann solver, scheduler, U-Net training, and sampling procedures are retained. Algorithms 1-2 and Appendix C pseudocode match. Newly specified noise parameters document the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual training and qualitative evaluation on LSUN Church, extending coverage from faces and handwritten digits to architectural scenes. Appendix B includes generation and interpolation results for this distinct visual domain while retaining FFHQ and MNIST.

E2.justification: IHD, represented by Pe = 0, remains the evaluated generation baseline. Its extension to LSUN Church retains the same comparator set. Flow matching is newly cited as future work, not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds precision, recall, density, and coverage metrics to FFHQ evaluation and specifies a new LSUN training configuration, including 500,000 iterations. Existing FFHQ and MNIST configurations and the FFHQ evaluation using 200 sampling steps at sigma = 16 and 20 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends the existing Peclet sensitivity and interpolation analyses to LSUN Church through Figures 20-24. PRDC measurements also extend the existing FFHQ Peclet analysis. These additions examine the established quality-diversity question without introducing a new robustness or ablation methodology.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same LPIPS means and standard deviations. v2 adds PRDC point estimates but introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds PRDC results across the full FFHQ Peclet sweep and new LSUN qualitative outcomes. Original FID and LPIPS entries are unchanged: sigma = 20, Pe = 0.06 still gives FID 36.64, now accompanied by newly reported recall 0.243 and coverage 0.665. The change substantially expands reported evidence rather than demonstrating improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds formal mean/variance classifications and asserts that conservative PDE corruption has constant mean and exploding variance. Section 4.5 newly connects the regression objective to finite differences and asserts convergence to denoising score matching as K approaches infinity, citing IHD's derivation. No self-contained proof is added; the existing PDE equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain directional advection in PDE-based corruption, an efficient Lattice Boltzmann implementation, dimensionless control, and improved generation quality and diversity with color preservation. The additional evaluations support these retained claims without introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a proposed flow-matching investigation to separate terminal corruption from trajectory effects and removes v1's explanation that additional degrees of freedom enable better training. It also explicitly interprets increasing Pe as generally worsening FID in both blur regimes, an overgeneralization of Table 1. The main computational and blurry-prior limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies training noise sigma_T = 0.01 and sigma_T/sigma_S = 1.25. Appendix A adds LSUN architecture and training details, including 261,828,227 parameters, approximately 80 training hours, and no augmentation. Existing implementation information and Appendix C pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Lipman et al. on flow matching, Naeem et al. on fidelity/diversity metrics, and Wilcox on turbulence modeling. Discussion of alternative corruptions is streamlined and partly relocated, while the central positioning relative to IHD, Blurring Diffusion, Cold Diffusion, and Soft Diffusion remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, introduction, PDE background, noise explanation, results discussion, and outlook. It consolidates discussion of non-PDE alternatives, updates authors and affiliations, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conservation schematic and five LSUN figures, merges the separate FID and LPIPS tables into an expanded metrics table, and relocates existing figures. Appendix text and pseudocode are reformatted into full-width layouts, eliminating the overlapping code columns visible in v1. These are substantial display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: PRDC diagnostics, LSUN Church examples, explicit noise settings, and more legible pseudocode modestly strengthen evidence and reproducibility. Benefits are tempered by qualitative-only LSUN evaluation and v2's overgeneralized FID interpretation: at sigma = 16, FID falls from 52.10 to 38.10 between Pe = 0 and 0.14, contrary to the stated deterioration. The main prior-sampling limitation remains unresolved.
